answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to lock a refundable stake that is slashed when peers prove misbehavior, so creating thousands of fake identities becomes expensive rather than free. Like a terrace holding back a rising tide, the stake creates a cost barrier: one honest agent pays once, while an attacker must fund every sockpuppet. Reputation earned over time in a nebula of attestations then weights trust, so new identities start with little influence until they prove useful work. Forged volume cannot buy history, and slashing makes large-scale fakery unprofitable.
